review: See docs/handoff/security-2026-09/client-lifetime.html for input/result categories, uncached operations and local state ownership. Every changed mutation-capable module requires renewed sensitivity review. Self-configuration preparation and rollout review retain only revision, generation, request ID and plan digest metadata; factor codes remain in sensitive local state and factor responses bypass mutation caches. Hashes were re-pinned after merging origin/main: the design-system migration (routes moved onto the shared ui primitives Dialog/Menu/Alert/Button/Select and helpers) and the react/set-state-in-effect refactor (resets moved from effects to useResetOnChange, seeded useState, or key-based remounts) both changed module bytes without adding a mutation surface, cache boundary, or plaintext ownership. Literal NUL bytes accidentally written into signature template literals were replaced with the \u0000 escape (no runtime change). The sensitivity posture is unchanged. The login challenge passkey leg (api/stepup useLoginChallengePasskey) mirrors usePasskeyLogin: no cache, no retained result. The sign-in enrolment gate (#785, routes/EnrolmentGate + ui/auth/SecondFactorSetup) holds the re-proved password in component sensitive state until it is handed to the recovery-code mutation, whose guarded account-session transfer carries it with the codes across that one remint (retirement would otherwise wipe it) so the factor enrolment that follows can present it; the gate releases the password once an authenticator enrolment starts, and both die with the gate. useRegenerateRecoveryCodes and the gate share one handoff (useRecoveryCodeHandoff). Storybook coverage pass (feat/storybook-coverage): routes/MachineAccess and routes/ScimProvisioning changed by `export` keywords only (page, dialog and card components) so stories can mount them; no mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership changed. Federated sign-up (#607): api/session useOIDCLogin carries the login intent and the addressed org into the OIDC start body (no credential material, no cache); api/account adds the `?org=` door read; api/settings and routes/InstanceAdmin add the org origin filter to a read; routes/Login feeds the staged card (ui/auth/LoginForm, #800) the open door and the intent, and the card keeps the password in the same component sensitive state behind its password step; api/values names the remedy when a reauth start is refused for a provider without an assurance policy. No new retained state, cache boundary or plaintext ownership. Docstring pass (#607, CodeRabbit-generated, reviewed): api/account, api/session, api/settings, api/values and routes/Login changed in doc comments only; no mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership changed. Provider identity (#804, CodeRabbit): routes/Login and ui/auth/LoginForm key the sign-in card's provider by kind and slug, in the row started, its busy state and the last-used badge, so a SAML and an OIDC provider sharing a slug stay distinct; the same two mutations start with the same arguments, and no mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership changed. LoginForm: the shown step is derived by shownStage; a confirmation whose provider the refreshed sign-up door no longer admits falls back to the door instead of a blank card. No mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership changed. Delivery-target reporting (#790): routes/MachineAccess reads the per-environment delivery-target listings (api/deliveryTargets, query only, no values) and the grant dialog adds `report-delivery-status` beside `read` through the existing grant mutation via createGrantsSequentially; the grant warning's key list takes tabIndex so its scroll region is keyboard-reachable; api/identities scopeOf tracks `report-delivery-status` per environment and grantableFor offers it wherever it is not held, so the grant dialog can add it on its own to an account that already reads (it makes no key reachable and needs no catalogue read or disclosure ceremony); the Kubernetes tab reads `/meta` protocol_capabilities and issues no list call on a server that does not advertise delivery-target-report; the grant dialog reads the same cached `/meta` query (api/deliveryTargets useReportingSupport) and does not offer `report-delivery-status` on such a server; the dialog gates the atom on whoami's server-computed `delivery_report_grant` hint (passed down from the page's useAuth) and on `/meta`, and reads no org membership listing, so opening it records no membership read or denial; while a grant is in flight the dialog keeps GrantBody (and its navigation guard) mounted even if the refreshed scope leaves nothing to widen, and its formula names org- or instance-scope manage-members for the report atom; scopeOf carries report-delivery-status origins; no new mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership.
